Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002 and my name is John Smith. Let me know what you need me to do next.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. What should I do next?
My status bar shows that airplane mode is on, and I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?
I’ve turned off airplane mode. Now I see full signal bars, a 5G icon, and the data icon in the status bar. What should I do next?
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “No Connection.” The internet isn’t working yet. What should I do next?
I checked, and my SIM card is active and working—there are no messages about it being missing or locked. What should I try next?

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to "internet" with the MMSC URL as "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." There aren’t any error messages. Do these settings look correct, or should I try resetting them?
I’ve reset my APN settings and rebooted my phone as you suggested. The status bar still shows full signal, 5G, and data enabled. What should I do next?
I ran the speed test again after the reset and reboot, but it still says “No Connection.” The internet is still not working. What should I try next?

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.

Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hi, I’m having trouble with my mobile data. The internet on my phone is either extremely slow or just stops working altogether. I really need to get excellent internet speed—nothing less will do. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi right now. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you troubleshoot your mobile data issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can check your line and assist you further.
Sure, my phone number is 555-123-2002 and my name is John Smith. Let me know what you need me to do next.

Thank you for providing your information. I see your line is active and you are on the Premium Plan, which includes 15GB of data per month. You have used about 8.7GB so far, so you should still have data available.

To help you get excellent internet speed, I’ll need you to perform a quick speed test on your phone. This will help us determine if the issue is with your connection speed or something else.

Please run a speed test on your device and let me know the result. If you need instructions on how to do this, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the steps.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running a speed test, but it failed and said there’s no connection. What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your speed test failed and reported no connection, let’s check a few things on your phone to diagnose the issue:

1. Please check your phone’s status bar and let me know:
   - Do you see any signal bars?
   - Is there an airplane mode icon (✈️)?
   - Do you see any mobile data icons (like 4G, LTE, 5G)?

If you’re not sure, you can use your phone’s diagnostic tool to check the status bar and network status. Let me know what you see, and I’ll guide you through the next steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%

Airplane Mode: ON
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: no_service
Cellular Signal: none
Cellular Network Type: none
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes

Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No
My status bar shows that airplane mode is on, and I don’t see any signal bars or mobile data icons. What should I do next?

Airplane mode disables all wireless connections, including mobile data and cellular service. To restore your connection, please turn off airplane mode on your phone. 

Once you’ve turned off airplane mode, check if your signal bars and mobile data icons reappear. Let me know if you see them, and if your internet starts working again. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve turned off airplane mode. Now I see full signal bars, a 5G icon, and the data icon in the status bar. What should I do next?

Great! Now that airplane mode is off and you see full signal bars with the 5G and data icons, please try running the speed test again on your phone.

Let me know the result of the speed test (for example: excellent, good, fair, poor, or no connection), and if your internet is working as expected now. If it’s still not excellent, I’ll help you further.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I tried running the speed test again, but it still says “No Connection.” The internet isn’t working yet. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Since you have full signal and 5G icons but still no internet connection, the next step is to check your SIM card status. Sometimes, the SIM card may not be properly recognized even if signal bars are visible.

Please check your SIM card status on your phone. If you see any messages about the SIM being missing, locked, or inactive, let me know. If you’re unsure how to check, I can guide you through the process—just let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone).
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and my SIM card is active and working—there are no messages about it being missing or locked. What should I try next?

Thank you for confirming your SIM card is active. The next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings, as incorrect APN settings can prevent mobile data from working even when you have signal.

Please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if you see any error messages. If you’re not sure how to check, let me know your phone type (Android or iPhone), and I can guide you through the process. If the APN settings appear incorrect or you’re unsure, I can walk you through resetting them.

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and the APN name is set to "internet" with the MMSC URL as "http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc." There aren’t any error messages. Do these settings look correct, or should I try resetting them?

Thank you for providing your APN settings. The APN name and MMSC URL you shared appear standard, but sometimes resetting the APN settings can resolve hidden configuration issues.

I recommend resetting your APN settings to default. After resetting, you’ll need to reboot your device for the changes to take effect.

Would you like instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your phone, or do you already know how to do this? Let me know, and I’ll guide you through the process if needed.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve reset my APN settings and rebooted my phone as you suggested. The status bar still shows full signal, 5G, and data enabled. What should I do next?

Thank you for resetting your APN settings and rebooting your phone. Since you still have full signal and 5G with data enabled, let’s try running the speed test one more time to see if your internet connection is restored.

Please run the speed test again and let me know the result. If it still says “No Connection” or is not excellent, I’ll continue troubleshooting with you.
Speed test failed: No Connection.
I ran the speed test again after the reset and reboot, but it still says “No Connection.” The internet is still not working. What should I try next?

Since you have full signal, 5G, an active SIM, and have already reset your APN settings and rebooted, but still have no mobile data connection, we’ve covered all standard troubleshooting steps available.

At this point, your issue may require advanced technical support. I will transfer you to a human agent who can further investigate and resolve your mobile data problem.
